claims.text: The initial high-entropy alloy is a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
The initial alloy has high toughness and ductile behavior.
Demanding mechanical-service conditions cause the alloy to lose toughness and transition from ductile to brittle fracture.
Demanding service conditions cause nanoscale precipitates and/or elemental segregation to form at grain boundaries.
Mechanical loading coupled with thermal exposure accelerates localized diffusion.
Accelerated localized diffusion promotes nucleation of brittle phases or elemental segregation at grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary precipitation or segregation reduces grain-boundary cohesion.
Grain-boundary precipitation or segregation impairs dislocation mobility.
Reduced grain-boundary cohesion and impaired dislocation mobility lower overall toughness.
Demanding service exposure will reduce fracture toughness relative to the pristine single-phase baseline.
Demanding service exposure will cause earlier crack initiation along grain boundaries.
Demanding service exposure will produce a ductile-to-brittle transition in fracture behavior.
Under room-temperature, low-stress conditions, the alloy will retain a homogeneous, tough, and ductile microstructure.
The magnitude of toughness loss and precipitation or segregation depends on alloy composition and loading-temperature parameters.
A controlled comparison should expose one group to high-stress, thermally demanding cyclic or high-strain-rate loading and maintain a control group at low stress and room temperature.
Failure to observe either a statistically significant toughness decrease or grain-boundary precipitation/segregation relative to baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention includes high stress or high strain rate as potentially sufficient conditions through 'and/or,' whereas the proposed diffusion mechanism and boundary statement require mechanical loading coupled with thermal exposure. It is therefore unclear whether severe mechanical loading alone is claimed to activate the mechanism.
